split_method: Temporal hold-out: features from days 8-14 predict days 15-21; trained models first learn days 1-7 -> 8-14. No random split (it would leak the future).
preprocessing_summary: Ticket stop names matched to GTFS stops (alias + fuzzy); load per stretch = ticketed passengers per scheduled trip (flow); cells need >= 10 tickets in the test week to count as truth; features: own earlier load (mF, nF), route average (rF), city average (gF), band, day type, position along the route, route length, scheduled trips, AC flag; Lasso / Logistic Regression use standardised features, missing history filled with 0.

thin_cell_comparison.note: Judged on all test cells with little history, not only cells that later turned out well observed (that filter would bias toward busy cells).

concepts.summary: Train on the past, test on a later week, as in real use.
concepts.example: Weeks 1-2 teach the model; week 3 is only used to score it.

concepts.summary: MAE is the average miss; RMSE punishes big misses; R² is the share of variation explained (0 = no better than the average).
concepts.example: MAE 0.26 means we are off by about a quarter of a ticketed passenger per trip.

concepts.summary: Linear regression with a penalty that pushes useless feature weights to exactly zero.
concepts.example: Features listed under lasso_zeroed_features carry no extra signal for Lasso.

concepts.summary: Both are many decision trees; forests average independent trees, boosting adds trees that fix earlier errors.
concepts.example: Trees capture 'busy only at 6 pm on this stretch', which a straight line cannot.

concepts.summary: Macro-F1 averages F1 over the three levels so the rare 'crowded' class counts equally; the matrix shows which levels get confused.
concepts.example: A 'standing' stretch predicted as 'seats' is a cell off the diagonal.

concepts.summary: Stretches with few tickets borrow strength from a model or from the route average, and are flagged with lower confidence.
concepts.example: prediction_source says observed_tickets, ml_fallback or route_average.
